hypothesis: A hierarchy of nested or multi-resolution families from one input, with evidence for two genes read as -log(size of the smallest shared cluster / N), serves both discovery (recurrence engine) and search; a flat partition is the one-level case.

common.engine: v1.5 statistics (deployed $RD/engine/code/recurrence.py), W = 3, genome-shuffle null, 3 replicates, rule = largest gene coverage at FDR <= 0.01, all-genome loci; scorer = package score_dpann_loci.py --min-members 2 (200 controls); comparison = dpann_compare.py (genome bootstrap, 2,000 draws, seed 17; tune = odd genome_code, test = even genome_code)
common.base: dpann__mmseqs__seq__e3c50s75__w3 ($RD/engine/results_dpann_v2), the reference of every earlier DPANN comparison
common.summed_excess: mean DefenseFinder excess + mean TXSScan excess (excess = best-locus F1 minus the mean F1 of 200 control placements)

T1.question: Does the V0 single-input arm (all 164,863,660 gene-level capped edges, weight = cosine similarity, Leiden modularity) beat the MMseqs2 base for Leiden seeds other than 17?
T1.resolution: 19000, chosen on odd genomes among the predeclared V0 controls r11000 / r15000 / r19000 / r23000 (tune summed excess vs base -0.011 / +0.012 / +0.033 / +0.028)
T1.also_run: seed 17 again (determinism check: identical memberships expected)
T1.criterion: confirmed if the even-genome summed excess difference to the base is >= +0.02 in at least 2 of the 3 new seeds
T1.reported_beside: F1 and excess for DefenseFinder, TXSScan and CRISPRCasTyper per seed
T1.refutation: fewer than 2 of 3 new seeds reach +0.02: the +0.038 of seed 17 was a seed-specific fluctuation and the single-input claim is not confirmed

attribution.design: descriptive 2 x 2 at matched token counts, low = 153,520 tokens (round-1 graph r3000, the best round-1 embedding-only arm, test summed -0.029) and high = 297,708 tokens (V0 r19000). Graph G1 = round-1 graph (mutual 20-NN of unique sequences from the IVF k50 file, nodes = unique sequences, weight cosine); G2 = V0 (gene-level edges: identical-sequence partners plus the HNSW k50 neighbours of each gene's sequence expanded to genes of other genomes, cap 64 per gene, undirected union). A third graph G3 = G2 restricted to its 56,962,567 mutual edges separates mutuality from gene-level expansion.
attribution.token_matching: for each graph a resolution grid; the run with the smallest |log(tokens / target)| represents the cell; the G1 run at resolution 19000 is also reported (resolution matched rather than granularity matched)
attribution.decomposition: graph effect at fixed granularity and granularity effect within a graph, both orders, with the interaction; no pass/fail criterion

T2.implementation: recurrence_ml.py, a copy of engine v1.5. Each gene carries one token per level. Every pair of genes within W on a contig is an instance at every level where both tokens are assigned and differ. Pair statistics (G, L, NP, J, E, P) are computed within each level exactly as v1.5. Each instance takes the level whose token pair has the smallest Poisson P (ties to the level listed first; levels listed by decreasing token count). Multiplicity over levels: the rules use P_adj = min(1, K * P) with K = number of levels, and the null applies the same per-instance choice after permuting gene order within each genome jointly for all levels (as --adaptive accounts for the window choice), so the empirical FDR includes the choice. Rules are evaluated on the token pairs (per level) selected by at least one instance. Support of a boundary = L of the selected pair of the best significant instance spanning it; loci are read from this combined support exactly as v1.5.
T2.reproduction_gate: with one level, recurrence_ml.py must reproduce the deployed v1.5 engine exactly on e3c50s75 at W = 3 (summary values other than timing, rules.tsv, significant_pairs, token_modules, boundary_support, loci_all_genomes) before any multi-level result is interpreted

c_both.B1: chosen E set + chosen S set

T2.selection: within each family the candidate with the highest odd-genome summed excess; best single level = the single level with the highest odd-genome summed excess within the same pool (a: the 8 V0 levels; b: the 3 MMseqs2 levels; c: all 11), all single levels run with the same engine
T2.criterion: for each of (a), (b), (c) separately: gain if on even genomes summed excess(chosen multi-level) - summed excess(chosen best single level) >= 0.02 with the paired genome-bootstrap 95% interval excluding 0, AND even-genome DefenseFinder F1 >= base - 0.01 AND even-genome TXSScan F1 >= base - 0.01
T2.refutation: no family meets the criterion: choosing one resolution well does as well as combining resolutions in the engine

T3.evidence: s(a, b) = max over levels l with tok_l(a) = tok_l(b) of log(N_db / n_l(a)), n_l(a) = genes of a's level-l cluster outside the query genome, N_db = genes outside the query genome (one level = M0 exactly). No per-query similarity search.
T3.protocol: round-1 locus search unchanged: windows of <= W = query span + wx genes (cap 60), greedy one-to-one slot filling, per-slot floor tau, circular-shift null with 200 replicates (seed 17 + qid), labels and AP as bench.py; DefenseFinder queries with >= 2 members; configuration chosen by mean primary AP on odd genomes (ties: smaller wx, larger tau); test on even genomes (1,247 queries with >= 1 relevant target)

H_emb (single source).L8: the 8 V0 levels of the T2 embedding pool

T3.references: frozen even-genome per-query metrics of M0 0.370, M2 0.576, S2 0.620, S3 0.698 ($RD/locus_search/out2/final_dfall_metrics.parquet); M0 unlabelled hits per query at E <= 0.01 = 0.719
T3.criterion: graded evidence without search: a single-source hierarchy (H_emb or H_seq, configuration chosen on odd genomes) reaches even-genome mean AP >= 0.576 at unlabelled hits per query (E <= 0.01) <= 1.5 x M0 (<= 1.079). Matches sequence search: the same with AP >= 0.620.
T3.refutation: both single-source hierarchies below 0.576 (or above the rate bound): hierarchy depth does not substitute for per-query graded ranks
T3.cost: CPU seconds per query for evidence assembly, scan and null, reported beside round-1 costs

T4.nestedness: for consecutive levels ordered by token count, the fraction of genes whose finer cluster lies entirely inside one coarser cluster
T4.nested_construction: top-down intersection: the coarsest level is kept; each finer level is replaced by its intersection with the nested level above it
T4.comparison: descriptive: the T2 chosen embedding set and the T3 chosen H_emb set rerun on nested levels; difference with paired interval
